question: In baseball, a batter who hits a high catchable ball is said to fly out. Yesterday, he did what?
answer: Flied out. Here fly is made from the noun a fly, short for fly ball, and a verb built from a noun takes the regular -ed, not the irregular past of the verb it resembles. The same logic gives a city ringed by troops, not rung, and a player who grandstanded.
move: Ask what a word is made from before deciding which rule it obeys.
trap: Fly already has the past tense flew, so flew out sounds right.
reference: Kim, Pinker, Prince & Prasada, Why no mere mortal has ever flown out to center field, Cognitive Science, 1991
